newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Rubber - SE Asian prices seen steady in slow trade.
newsitem.headline: Rubber - SE Asian prices seen steady in slow trade.

text.p: Regional rubber prices will probably trend steady to easier this week because of soft buying sentiment, Southeast Asian rubber traders said on Monday.
The weak sentiment will more than offset the recent move up by the Japanese market and mild Chinese and European short-covering last week, the traders said.
Supplies may also be boosted by improving weather in Malaysia and Thailand, which may knock sentiment lower.
Prices will also be weighed down by a holiday on Monday in the rubber markets of Kuala Lumpur and Singapore, they said.
"You're probably looking at more of a range-trading scenario this week," said a senior dealer at a Western commodity house.
"There's been a little Chinese and European buying, but we're still in...a bear market."
"If the weather improves further, prices will slowly drift downwards," another Singapore-based trader said. "There's been some short-covering by European consumers, but trading will likely be slow."
Indonesian dealers said trading was thin last week as foreign buyers stayed on the sidelines waiting for prices to weaken.
"I think prices could weaken a little this week if buyers continue to stay out," one dealer said. "Their (buyers) bids last week have mostly been lower than offer prices."
One factor which could shore up prices would be a further weakening of the Japanese yen against the U.S. dollar.
The weak yen helped lift Tokyo rubber futures on Friday.
"Our market usually takes its cue from Tokyo, and if prices there continue to rise, prices here will be steady," one said.
Tyre-grade December/January delivery SIR20 offer prices finished last week at 56.00-56.50 U.S. cents/lb FOB Medan, unchanged from the previous week.
RSS1 was last done at 130 cents/kg, up from 125.50 cents the previous week's while dry latex was 2,300-400 rupiah/kg against 2,200 rupiah.
Malaysian traders said they expected prices to move in a tight range this week if consumer demand remained thin.
"There's no indication that buyers are going to flood the market yet," said a Kuala Lumpur-based dealer. "The market's mostly seen price adjustments and maybe some short-covering."
The dealer said he expected the benchmark RSS1, which the Malaysian Rubber Exchange and Licensing Board quoted at 321 Malaysian cents per kg on Friday, to remain largely unchanged.
SMR20 could gain between four and five cents this week, one dealer said. It was at 310.50 Malaysian cents at the close of the previous week.

Another dealer said supply of raw materials, especially latex, was expected to dwindle this week with the country's army of Hindu rubber tappers taking long holidays to celebrate Deepavali, the Hindu New Year.
"Some could be off the whole of next week and this is going to have some impact on production," said the dealer.
The Malaysian rubber market has been languishing from weak consumer demand since September, except for some short-covering of SMR20 and latex.
Offer prices for latex rose five cents on Friday to 240 cents per kg after short-covering by local agents for earlier positions sold to China.
Thai rubber prices will probably move in a very narrow range as actual demand remains limited, trade sources said.
Thai benchmark RSS3 for December shipment was quoted around US$1.24-1.26 a kg FOB Bangkok against $1.23-1.25 a kg.
STR20 for the same shipment was quoted around $1.24 on Friday, campared with $1.22 the previous week. Latex was unchanged at 95 U.S. cents a kg.
"There are some inquiries and buying interest, especially from China. But actual buying was moderate," a Thai trader said.
(With contributions from Thailand, Malaysia and Indonesia)
-- Singapore newsroom (65 8703305)
